title: What an audit compares

blocks.text: The same planning service stores a record of each solve, so that an auditor's rerun can be compared with the original. A record must hold only what a repeatable run repeats, and it must be the same for two builds of the same model.
Write `record(solver, status, pick)` in `audit.py`, where `pick` maps each feeder's name to its Boolean variable. Return a tuple of three items:

items: the objective value as a whole number, an `int`: `round(solver.objective_value)`, as the reference does. `solver.objective_value` is a float that can land just below the whole number (lesson 4.5.3), and `int(...)` would then cut it down by one;
the names of the feeders the solution picks, as a tuple in alphabetical order.

blocks.text: Leave out anything that measures the clock. About three lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


def record(solver: cp_model.CpSolver, status, pick: dict[str, cp_model.IntVar]) -> tuple:
    """What a repeatable run is compared on: status name, objective, and the chosen names in order."""
    chosen = tuple(sorted(name for name, var in pick.items() if solver.value(var)))
    return (solver.status_name(status), round(solver.objective_value), chosen)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    pick = {name: model.new_bool_var(name) for name in ("b", "a")}
    model.add(sum(pick.values()) <= 1)
    model.maximize(2 * pick["a"] + pick["b"])
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1
    print(record(solver, solver.solve(model), pick))

import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model

from audit import record

# Four pole upgrades, (cost, gain), and a budget.
upgrades = {"P4": (30, 40), "P2": (25, 38), "P3": (20, 22), "P1": (35, 50)}
def run(budget):
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    pick = {n: model.new_bool_var(n) for n in upgrades}
    model.add(sum(c * pick[n] for n, (c, _) in upgrades.items()) <= budget)
    model.maximize(sum(g * pick[n] for n, (_, g) in upgrades.items()))
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1
    solver.parameters.random_seed = 4
    return record(solver, solver.solve(model), pick)


print("record at budget 70:", run(70))
print("record at budget 70, run again:", run(70))
print("record at budget 45:", run(45))

cases.says: two repeatable runs of the same model give equal records
the record is the status name, the objective as a whole number and the chosen names
a model that makes its variables in another order gives the same record

origin.section: One Worker, a Fixed Seed and a Deterministic Limit Repeat Every Number but the Clock

concepts: a run is compared on the fields that repeat, in an order that does not depend on how the model was built
